newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINA'S FERNANDEZ PREDICTS RECORD '97 ECONOMY.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINA'S FERNANDEZ PREDICTS RECORD '97 ECONOMY.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez predicted Wednesday bank deposits and lending, in addition to oil, gas, electricity and industrial production, will all hit records levels in 1997.
In an article signed by Fernandez published by state news agency Telam, the minister also said direct foreign investment would surpass $7 billion this year, up from $5 billion last year.

He said deposits in the financial system in June stood at $63 billion, a jump of 25 percent from the same month a year earlier. Bank loans, meanwhile, rose 15 percent in the same period to $55 billion in June.
"Few times before has Argentina been so well prepared for the demands and the challenges of globaization," Ferandez wrote.
He said growth is set to reach seven percent this year, while the budget deficit is set to continue declining to $1.5 billion in 1998 from $3.0 billion this year and $6.0 billion in 1996.

"The figures are positive. Now, the most important thing is to persist and consolidate the economic transformation...to achieve what all Argentines want: reach high rates of growth so that the whole population can enjoy the benefits of welfare," he said. To further the reforms, "the reduction of tax evasion and labor market modernization are our two big objectives."
He said that if deep labor market reforms were achieved, in a few years unemployment would likely fall to a single digit number from its current 16.1 percent level.
